claim: β-Propellers arise through the amplification of a supersecondary structure element called a blade.
source: β-Propellers arise through the amplification of a supersecondary structure element called a blade.
evidence: This is a foundational statement about β-propeller structure that is presented as established knowledge in the field.

claim: β-Propellers produce toroids of between four and twelve repeats.
source: This process produces toroids of between four and twelve repeats, which are almost always arranged sequentially in a single polypeptide chain.
evidence: This is stated as an established fact about the range of blade numbers in β-propellers.

claim: β-Propeller repeats are almost always arranged sequentially in a single polypeptide chain.
source: This process produces toroids of between four and twelve repeats, which are almost always arranged sequentially in a single polypeptide chain.
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge about the typical arrangement of propeller blades.

claim: New propellers evolve continuously by amplification from single blades.
source: We found that new propellers evolve continuously by amplification from single blades.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the authors' previous work, supported by citation to their bioinformatic studies.

claim: One- to six-bladed building blocks derived from two seven-bladed WD40 propellers yielded stable homo-oligomers with six to nine blades.
source: One- to six-bladed building blocks derived from two seven-bladed WD40 propellers yielded stable homo-oligomers with six to nine blades, depending on the size of the building block.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding of the study, supported by biophysical characterization data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The number of blades in oligomeric propellers depends on the size of the building block.
source: One- to six-bladed building blocks derived from two seven-bladed WD40 propellers yielded stable homo-oligomers with six to nine blades, depending on the size of the building block.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the study's data.

claim: High-resolution structures were obtained for tetramers of two blades, trimers of three blades, and dimers of four and five blades.
source: High-resolution structures for tetramers of two blades, trimers of three blades, and dimers of four and five blades, respectively, show structurally diverse propellers and include a novel fold, highlighting the inherent flexibility of the WD40 blade.
evidence: This is stated as a result and supported by crystallographic data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The oligomeric propeller structures show structural diversity.
source: High-resolution structures for tetramers of two blades, trimers of three blades, and dimers of four and five blades, respectively, show structurally diverse propellers and include a novel fold, highlighting the inherent flexibility of the WD40 blade.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the crystallographic structures obtained in the study.

claim: The oligomeric propeller structures include a novel fold.
source: High-resolution structures for tetramers of two blades, trimers of three blades, and dimers of four and five blades, respectively, show structurally diverse propellers and include a novel fold, highlighting the inherent flexibility of the WD40 blade.
evidence: This is stated as a finding and supported by the crystallographic structure of the 5-bladed dimer.

claim: The structural diversity highlights the inherent flexibility of the WD40 blade.
source: High-resolution structures for tetramers of two blades, trimers of three blades, and dimers of four and five blades, respectively, show structurally diverse propellers and include a novel fold, highlighting the inherent flexibility of the WD40 blade.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the structural data obtained in the study.

claim: Subdomain-sized fragments can provide structural versatility in the evolution of new proteins.
source: Our data support the hypothesis that subdomain-sized fragments can provide structural versatility in the evolution of new proteins.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion supported by the experimental data presented in the study.

claim: Current evolutionary scenarios generally treat domains as the unit of protein evolution.
source: Current evolutionary scenarios generally treat domains as the unit of protein evolution.
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge in the field of protein evolution.

claim: Domains display a level of complexity that seems to preclude their origin by chemical processes in an abiotic environment.
source: Domains, however, already display a level of complexity that seems to preclude their origin by chemical processes in an abiotic environment.
evidence: This is presented as a reasoning for the authors' evolutionary model.

claim: The first domains evolved from a pool of peptides with the propensity to form supersecondary structures.
source: We have proposed that the first domains evolved from a pool of peptides with the propensity to form supersecondary structures, which originated in the context of RNA-based replication and catalysis (Lupas et al., 2001; Söding and Lupas, 2003).
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis proposed by the authors in previous work.

claim: The ancestral peptides originated in the context of RNA-based replication and catalysis.
source: We have proposed that the first domains evolved from a pool of peptides with the propensity to form supersecondary structures, which originated in the context of RNA-based replication and catalysis (Lupas et al., 2001; Söding and Lupas, 2003).
evidence: This is part of the authors' evolutionary model cited from their previous work.

claim: Initially, ancestral peptides were entirely dependent on an RNA scaffold for their structure and activity.
source: Initially, these peptides were entirely dependent on an RNA scaffold for their structure and activity, but increasing complexity allowed them to form structures by excluding water through hydrophobic contacts and thus gain independence from RNA; in this model, protein folding was an emergent property of peptide-RNA coevolution (Lupas and Alva, 2017).
evidence: This is part of the authors' evolutionary model cited from their previous work.

claim: Increasing complexity allowed ancestral peptides to form structures by excluding water through hydrophobic contacts and gain independence from RNA.
source: Initially, these peptides were entirely dependent on an RNA scaffold for their structure and activity, but increasing complexity allowed them to form structures by excluding water through hydrophobic contacts and thus gain independence from RNA; in this model, protein folding was an emergent property of peptide-RNA coevolution (Lupas and Alva, 2017).
evidence: This is part of the authors' evolutionary model cited from their previous work.

claim: Protein folding was an emergent property of peptide-RNA coevolution.
source: Initially, these peptides were entirely dependent on an RNA scaffold for their structure and activity, but increasing complexity allowed them to form structures by excluding water through hydrophobic contacts and thus gain independence from RNA; in this model, protein folding was an emergent property of peptide-RNA coevolution (Lupas and Alva, 2017).
evidence: This is stated as part of the authors' evolutionary model.

claim: 40 ancestral peptides have been computationally retraced whose presence in different folds suggests they predated the first folded proteins.
source: Using a computational approach, we have retraced 40 of these peptides, whose presence in different folds suggests that they predated the first folded proteins (Alva et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the authors' previous computational work.

claim: The nucleotide-binding helix-turn-helix motif is found in 14 different folds.
source: The most prolific, such as the nucleotide-binding helix-turn-helix motif, found in 14 different folds (Sauer et al., 1982; Steitz et al., 1982; Rosinski and Atchley, 1999; Aravind et al., 2005), or the (di)nucleotide-binding β-α-β Rossmann motif, found in 10 different folds (Rossmann et al., 1974; Dym and Eisenberg, 2001; Laurino et al., 2016), illustrate a fundamental property of these ancestral peptides: while deterministic with respect to their own structure, they are sufficiently flexible to have given rise to topologically different folds (Copley et al., 2001; Grishin, 2001; Krishna et al., 2006; Alva et al., 2008; Pereira and Lupas, 2018b).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: The (di)nucleotide-binding β-α-β Rossmann motif is found in 10 different folds.
source: The most prolific, such as the nucleotide-binding helix-turn-helix motif, found in 14 different folds (Sauer et al., 1982; Steitz et al., 1982; Rosinski and Atchley, 1999; Aravind et al., 2005), or the (di)nucleotide-binding β-α-β Rossmann motif, found in 10 different folds (Rossmann et al., 1974; Dym and Eisenberg, 2001; Laurino et al., 2016), illustrate a fundamental property of these ancestral peptides: while deterministic with respect to their own structure, they are sufficiently flexible to have given rise to topologically different folds (Copley et al., 2001; Grishin, 2001; Krishna et al., 2006; Alva et al., 2008; Pereira and Lupas, 2018b).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: Ancestral peptides are deterministic with respect to their own structure but sufficiently flexible to have given rise to topologically different folds.
source: The most prolific, such as the nucleotide-binding helix-turn-helix motif, found in 14 different folds (Sauer et al., 1982; Steitz et al., 1982; Rosinski and Atchley, 1999; Aravind et al., 2005), or the (di)nucleotide-binding β-α-β Rossmann motif, found in 10 different folds (Rossmann et al., 1974; Dym and Eisenberg, 2001; Laurino et al., 2016), illustrate a fundamental property of these ancestral peptides: while deterministic with respect to their own structure, they are sufficiently flexible to have given rise to topologically different folds (Copley et al., 2001; Grishin, 2001; Krishna et al., 2006; Alva et al., 2008; Pereira and Lupas, 2018b).
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the data on ancestral peptides, supported by citations.

claim: A four-stranded β-meander is found in β-propellers, β-prisms, and in the luminal domain of IRE1.
source: In this paper, we attempt to track some of this structural versatility in one of the fragments we retraced, a four-stranded β-meander found in β-propellers, β-prisms, and in the luminal domain of IRE1 (Kopec and Lupas, 2013).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the authors' previous work on ancestral fragments.

claim: Peptides can achieve an increase in complexity through self-association by homo-oligomerization or by amplification into a repetitive array on a single polypeptide chain.
source: The simplest way for peptides to achieve an increase in complexity is self-association, either by homo-oligomerization, or by amplification into a repetitive array on a single polypeptide chain (Eck and Dayhoff, 1966; McLachlan, 1972; McLachlan, 1987; Remmert et al., 2010; Smock et al., 2016; Zhu et al., 2016; Franklin et al., 2018; Pereira and Lupas, 2018a).
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge in protein evolution, supported by multiple citations.

claim: Many folds spanning all levels of complexity clearly originated through self-association.
source: Many folds, spanning all levels of complexity (fibrous, solenoid, toroid, and globular), clearly originated in this way.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in protein evolution.

claim: β-Propellers offer an attractive model system to study the process of peptide self-association.
source: β-Propellers offer an attractive model system to study this process (Nikkhah et al., 2006; Yadid and Tawfik, 2007; Chaudhuri et al., 2008; Yadid et al., 2010; Yadid and Tawfik, 2011; Voet et al., 2014; Smock et al., 2016; Noguchi et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated as a rationale for the study, supported by citations to previous work.

claim: β-Propellers are toroids formed by sequential supersecondary structure units of typically 40–50 residues.
source: They are toroids formed by sequential supersecondary structure units of typically 40–50 residues, each consisting of four anti-parallel β-strands.
evidence: This is presented as established structural knowledge about β-propellers.

claim: Each β-propeller blade consists of four anti-parallel β-strands.
source: They are toroids formed by sequential supersecondary structure units of typically 40–50 residues, each consisting of four anti-parallel β-strands.
evidence: This is presented as established structural knowledge about β-propeller blades.

claim: β-Propeller blades are arranged radially with their strands perpendicular to the plane of the toroid.
source: The units are arranged radially, with their strands perpendicular to the plane of the toroid, and have a right-handed twist, hence the name 'propeller' for the fold and 'blades' for the repetitive units.
evidence: This is presented as established structural knowledge about β-propellers.

claim: β-Propeller blades have a right-handed twist.
source: The units are arranged radially, with their strands perpendicular to the plane of the toroid, and have a right-handed twist, hence the name 'propeller' for the fold and 'blades' for the repetitive units.
evidence: This is presented as established structural knowledge about β-propellers.

claim: Up to three strands of the last blade are often circularly permuted to the N-terminus of the propeller.
source: Often up to three strands of the last blade are circularly permuted to the N‐terminus of the propeller, resulting in a 'velcro' closure via hydrogen bonding of the N- and C-terminal strands within the same blade (see Figure 1B), an arrangement that is thought to provide increased stability and folding specificity (Neer and Smith, 1996).
evidence: This is presented as established structural knowledge about β-propellers, supported by citation and reference to a figure.

claim: The velcro closure is thought to provide increased stability and folding specificity.
source: Often up to three strands of the last blade are circularly permuted to the N‐terminus of the propeller, resulting in a 'velcro' closure via hydrogen bonding of the N- and C-terminal strands within the same blade (see Figure 1B), an arrangement that is thought to provide increased stability and folding specificity (Neer and Smith, 1996).
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis from the literature, supported by citation.

claim: Propellers can differ considerably in their number of blades, with structures of between four and twelve blades currently deposited in the PDB.
source: Although all blades are structurally very similar, propellers can differ considerably in their number of blades, with structures of between four and twelve blades currently deposited in the Protein Data Bank (PDB).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the PDB database.

claim: Propellers span the full range of internal symmetry, from near sequence identity of their blades to full differentiation.
source: Also, uniquely among toroids, propellers span the full range of internal symmetry, from near sequence identity of their blades to full differentiation, where the similarity of the blades is essentially only recognizable from their structure.
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge about propeller diversity.

claim: Propellers are unique among toroids in spanning the full range of internal symmetry.
source: Also, uniquely among toroids, propellers span the full range of internal symmetry, from near sequence identity of their blades to full differentiation, where the similarity of the blades is essentially only recognizable from their structure.
evidence: This is stated as a distinguishing feature of propellers compared to other toroidal structures.

claim: Propellers can have enzymatic activity, bind ligands, or mediate protein–protein interactions.
source: Diversity in sequence and structure extends to diversity in function; propellers can have enzymatic activity, bind ligands, or mediate protein–protein interactions.
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge about propeller functions.

claim: Propellers often perform their function as a domain in the context of a larger protein.
source: Often, they perform their function as a domain in the context of a larger protein.
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge about propeller architecture in proteins.

claim: New propellers arise from single blades by amplification and differentiation.
source: Using bioinformatic and phylogenetic tools, we have previously shown that new propellers arise from single blades by amplification and differentiation, and that the common ancestor of the major propeller lineages was a single blade, not a fully formed propeller (Chaudhuri et al., 2008; Kopec and Lupas, 2013).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the authors' previous bioinformatic work.

claim: The common ancestor of the major propeller lineages was a single blade, not a fully formed propeller.
source: Using bioinformatic and phylogenetic tools, we have previously shown that new propellers arise from single blades by amplification and differentiation, and that the common ancestor of the major propeller lineages was a single blade, not a fully formed propeller (Chaudhuri et al., 2008; Kopec and Lupas, 2013).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the authors' previous bioinformatic work.

claim: Nikkhah et al. (2006) used a consensus WD40 blade to generate proteins with between 4 and 10 repeats, but none appeared folded or oligomeric.
source: The first was conducted by Nikkhah et al. (2006), who used a consensus WD40 blade to generate proteins with between 4 and 10 repeats, but none of the constructs appeared folded or oligomeric.
evidence: This is stated as a summary of findings from a cited study.

claim: Groups in Israel and Japan built folded, oligomeric propellers from the 5-bladed tachylectin-2 propeller and from a 6-bladed NHL propeller.
source: Subsequently, groups in Israel and Japan built folded, oligomeric propellers from the 5-bladed tachylectin-2 propeller and from a 6-bladed NHL propeller, respectively (Yadid et al., 2010; Voet et al., 2014; Smock et al., 2016), but all their constructs reproduced the parental fold, suggesting that the number of blades in the final structure is not flexible, although it can be reached through oligomeric intermediates.
evidence: This is stated as a summary of findings from cited studies.

claim: All constructs from the tachylectin-2 and NHL propeller studies reproduced the parental fold.
source: Subsequently, groups in Israel and Japan built folded, oligomeric propellers from the 5-bladed tachylectin-2 propeller and from a 6-bladed NHL propeller, respectively (Yadid et al., 2010; Voet et al., 2014; Smock et al., 2016), but all their constructs reproduced the parental fold, suggesting that the number of blades in the final structure is not flexible, although it can be reached through oligomeric intermediates.
evidence: This is stated as a summary of findings from cited studies.

claim: Previous studies suggested that the number of blades in the final structure is not flexible, although it can be reached through oligomeric intermediates.
source: Subsequently, groups in Israel and Japan built folded, oligomeric propellers from the 5-bladed tachylectin-2 propeller and from a 6-bladed NHL propeller, respectively (Yadid et al., 2010; Voet et al., 2014; Smock et al., 2016), but all their constructs reproduced the parental fold, suggesting that the number of blades in the final structure is not flexible, although it can be reached through oligomeric intermediates.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of findings from cited studies.

claim: None of the WRAP constructs reproduced the parental structure.
source: In contrast to the other studies, none of our constructs reproduced the parental structure, instead yielding a diversity of forms, in an extreme case even giving rise to an arguably novel fold.
evidence: This is stated as a primary finding of the study, contrasting with previous work.

claim: The WRAP constructs yielded a diversity of forms.
source: In contrast to the other studies, none of our constructs reproduced the parental structure, instead yielding a diversity of forms, in an extreme case even giving rise to an arguably novel fold.
evidence: This is stated as a primary finding of the study.

claim: In an extreme case, the WRAP constructs gave rise to an arguably novel fold.
source: In contrast to the other studies, none of our constructs reproduced the parental structure, instead yielding a diversity of forms, in an extreme case even giving rise to an arguably novel fold.
evidence: This is stated as a primary finding of the study.

claim: The high-resolution structures reveal the geometrical adjustments that the repeat units undergo to enable structural flexibility.
source: Their high-resolution structures reveal the geometrical adjustments that the repeat units have to undergo to enable this structural flexibility.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the crystallographic analysis.

claim: At the start of the project, the WD40 propeller with the highest internal sequence symmetry was the C-terminal domain of PkwA from Thermomonospora curvata.
source: At the start of the project, the WD40 propeller with the highest internal sequence symmetry was the C-terminal domain of the putative serine/threonine protein kinase PkwA from the thermophilic actinobacterium Thermomonospora curvata (GenBank: AAB05822.1), whose blades mostly share >60% pairwise identity (Figure 1A), unreported in any propeller before (Janda et al., 1996).
evidence: This is stated as a rationale for choosing PkwA, supported by sequence analysis shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The blades of PkwA mostly share >60% pairwise identity.
source: At the start of the project, the WD40 propeller with the highest internal sequence symmetry was the C-terminal domain of the putative serine/threonine protein kinase PkwA from the thermophilic actinobacterium Thermomonospora curvata (GenBank: AAB05822.1), whose blades mostly share >60% pairwise identity (Figure 1A), unreported in any propeller before (Janda et al., 1996).
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of PkwA, supported by the alignment shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The level of sequence identity in PkwA blades was unreported in any propeller before.
source: At the start of the project, the WD40 propeller with the highest internal sequence symmetry was the C-terminal domain of the putative serine/threonine protein kinase PkwA from the thermophilic actinobacterium Thermomonospora curvata (GenBank: AAB05822.1), whose blades mostly share >60% pairwise identity (Figure 1A), unreported in any propeller before (Janda et al., 1996).
evidence: This is stated as a distinguishing feature of PkwA, supported by citation.

claim: Expression was obtained for all PkwA constructs except the six-bladed construct.
source: We recombinantly expressed the constructs in E. coli and obtained expression for all but the six-bladed construct.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result.

claim: The single-bladed PkwA fragment was an unfolded monomer.
source: By far-UV circular dichroism (CD), tryptophan fluorescence spectroscopy, static light scattering (SLS), and native polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (PAGE), we observed that the fragment comprising merely a single blade was an unfolded monomer, whereas all other fragments appeared to form folded homo-oligomers (Table 1 upper panel; Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result from biophysical characterization.

claim: All PkwA fragments except the single-bladed construct appeared to form folded homo-oligomers.
source: By far-UV circular dichroism (CD), tryptophan fluorescence spectroscopy, static light scattering (SLS), and native polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (PAGE), we observed that the fragment comprising merely a single blade was an unfolded monomer, whereas all other fragments appeared to form folded homo-oligomers (Table 1 upper panel; Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result from biophysical characterization.

claim: The 2-bladed PkwA construct formed tetramers, suggesting an 8-bladed propeller.
source: The 2-bladed construct formed tetramers, suggesting an 8-bladed propeller and the 3-bladed, 4-bladed, and 5-bladed constructs formed dimers, suggesting the formation of 6-bladed, 8-bladed, and 10-bladed propellers, respectively.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result and interpretation.

claim: The 3-bladed, 4-bladed, and 5-bladed PkwA constructs formed dimers.
source: The 2-bladed construct formed tetramers, suggesting an 8-bladed propeller and the 3-bladed, 4-bladed, and 5-bladed constructs formed dimers, suggesting the formation of 6-bladed, 8-bladed, and 10-bladed propellers, respectively.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result.

claim: The authors were unable to obtain high-resolution structures for any of the PkwA oligomers.
source: We were, however, unable to obtain high-resolution structures for any of these oligomers, evidence which we considered essential in order to judge whether such structural diversity had indeed been obtained.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the PkwA experiments.

claim: In the case of the 5-bladed tachylectin propeller, fragments with two blades reproduced the structure of the parent by forming pentamers.
source: For comparison, in the case of the 5-bladed tachylectin propeller, fragments with two blades reproduced the structure of the parent by forming pentamers, which assembled into two 5-bladed propellers (Yadid et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated as a comparison to previous work, supported by citation.

claim: All constructs derived from a symmetrized version of the 6-bladed NHL propeller PknD reproduced the structure of the parent by assembling into higher-order oligomers.
source: Similarly, all constructs derived from a symmetrized version of the 6-bladed NHL propeller PknD reproduced the structure of the parent by assembling into higher-order oligomers (Voet et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as a comparison to previous work, supported by citation.

claim: None of the PkwA assemblies appear to have reproduced the parental structure.
source: In contrast, none of our assemblies appear to have taken this path to reproduce the parental structure.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: The authors were unable to obtain hetero-oligomers with seven blades by mixing PkwA constructs with different numbers of blades.
source: We therefore mixed constructs with different numbers of blades in an attempt to generate hetero-oligomers with seven blades, but were unable to obtain any, either by co-expression or in vitro mixtures of purified components in defined stoichiometries.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result.

claim: The PkwA fragments only reassembled efficiently into the original homo-oligomers.
source: The fragments only reassembled efficiently into the original homo-oligomers (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Three single-bladed PkwA constructs behaved as monomers with spectra characteristic of unfolded or partially folded peptides under all tested conditions.
source: However, under all tested conditions, the three single-bladed PkwA constructs behaved as monomers with spectra characteristic of unfolded or partially folded peptides.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result from biophysical characterization.

claim: WRAP is found in the C-terminal part of Npun_R6612 from Nostoc punctiforme PCC 73102.
source: Since none of our single-bladed PkwA constructs were folded, we turned our attention to another highly symmetric β-propeller of the WD40 family, found in the C-terminal part of Npun_R6612 from the multicellular cyanobacterium Nostoc punctiforme PCC 73102 and referred to henceforth as WRAP (WD40-family Recently Amplified Propeller; ACC84870.1).
evidence: This is stated as background information about WRAP.

claim: WRAP was identified during a systematic bioinformatic survey of β-propellers.
source: WRAP, which we identified during a systematic bioinformatic survey of β-propellers (Chaudhuri et al., 2008), was particularly interesting in that its 14 blades are practically identical (Figure 2A), having acquired only 10 point mutations over 563 residues (6 of these being Trp → Arg mutations at the same position of blades 1, 3, 6, 10, 12, and 13), as a result of 13 non-synonymous substitutions at the DNA level (Dunin-Horkawicz et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as background information about WRAP, supported by citations.

claim: WRAP's 14 blades are practically identical.
source: WRAP, which we identified during a systematic bioinformatic survey of β-propellers (Chaudhuri et al., 2008), was particularly interesting in that its 14 blades are practically identical (Figure 2A), having acquired only 10 point mutations over 563 residues (6 of these being Trp → Arg mutations at the same position of blades 1, 3, 6, 10, 12, and 13), as a result of 13 non-synonymous substitutions at the DNA level (Dunin-Horkawicz et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of WRAP, supported by the alignment in Figure 2A and citation.

claim: WRAP has acquired only 10 point mutations over 563 residues.
source: WRAP, which we identified during a systematic bioinformatic survey of β-propellers (Chaudhuri et al., 2008), was particularly interesting in that its 14 blades are practically identical (Figure 2A), having acquired only 10 point mutations over 563 residues (6 of these being Trp → Arg mutations at the same position of blades 1, 3, 6, 10, 12, and 13), as a result of 13 non-synonymous substitutions at the DNA level (Dunin-Horkawicz et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of WRAP, supported by citation.

claim: 6 of the 10 point mutations in WRAP are Trp → Arg mutations at the same position of blades 1, 3, 6, 10, 12, and 13.
source: WRAP, which we identified during a systematic bioinformatic survey of β-propellers (Chaudhuri et al., 2008), was particularly interesting in that its 14 blades are practically identical (Figure 2A), having acquired only 10 point mutations over 563 residues (6 of these being Trp → Arg mutations at the same position of blades 1, 3, 6, 10, 12, and 13), as a result of 13 non-synonymous substitutions at the DNA level (Dunin-Horkawicz et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of WRAP, supported by citation.

claim: The mutations in WRAP are a result of 13 non-synonymous substitutions at the DNA level.
source: WRAP, which we identified during a systematic bioinformatic survey of β-propellers (Chaudhuri et al., 2008), was particularly interesting in that its 14 blades are practically identical (Figure 2A), having acquired only 10 point mutations over 563 residues (6 of these being Trp → Arg mutations at the same position of blades 1, 3, 6, 10, 12, and 13), as a result of 13 non-synonymous substitutions at the DNA level (Dunin-Horkawicz et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of WRAP, supported by citation.

claim: The 14 blades of WRAP assemble into two 7-bladed β-propellers.
source: The 14 blades assemble into two 7-bladed β-propellers (PDB: 2YMU; Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated as structural information about WRAP, supported by reference to the PDB structure and Figure 2B.

claim: A single blade of WRAP (residues 670–710) showed no folding when recombinantly expressed.
source: We recombinantly expressed one blade of WRAP (residues 670–710) but yet again, as for our other single-blade constructs, obtained no folding.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result.

claim: The WRAP domain was clearly amplified extremely recently, as judged from the near identity of its constituent blades and the absence of any synonymous mutations in the DNA encoding them.
source: The WRAP domain was clearly amplified extremely recently, as judged from the near identity of its constituent blades and the absence of any synonymous mutations in the DNA encoding them (Dunin-Horkawicz et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the sequence data, supported by citation.

claim: All WRAP constructs (2-6 blades) were successfully expressed in E. coli and could be purified.
source: We therefore used the aforementioned single WRAP blade to probe the foldability of fragments with tandem repeats of two to six blades (see Figure 2—figure supplement 1 for sequences). All constructs were successfully expressed in E. coli and could be purified for further analysis.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result.

claim: The WRAP complexes unfolded thermally in a cooperative fashion, indicative of well-folded proteins.
source: In CD experiments, the complexes unfolded thermally in a cooperative fashion, indicative of well-folded proteins, and their tryptophan fluorescence spectra also resembled those of folded proteins (Table 1).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result from CD spectroscopy.

claim: The tryptophan fluorescence spectra of WRAP complexes resembled those of folded proteins.
source: In CD experiments, the complexes unfolded thermally in a cooperative fashion, indicative of well-folded proteins, and their tryptophan fluorescence spectra also resembled those of folded proteins (Table 1).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result from fluorescence spectroscopy.

claim: The 2-bladed WRAP construct behaved as a single species in solution.
source: The 2-bladed construct behaved as a single species in solution, but size determination by SLS and analytical gel size exclusion chromatography did not allow us to unequivocally distinguish between a trimeric and tetrameric form (Table 1).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result.

claim: Size determination by SLS and analytical gel size exclusion chromatography did not allow unequivocal distinction between a trimeric and tetrameric form for the 2-bladed WRAP construct.
source: The 2-bladed construct behaved as a single species in solution, but size determination by SLS and analytical gel size exclusion chromatography did not allow us to unequivocally distinguish between a trimeric and tetrameric form (Table 1).
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the experimental methods.

claim: All WRAP fragments tended to dissociate during native polyacrylamide electrophoresis.
source: Moreover, as all WRAP fragments tended to dissociate during native polyacrylamide electrophoresis, we could not use this as an additional criterion for assessing the state of the assembly, as we had done for the PkwA constructs.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental observation.

claim: Glutaraldehyde crosslinking was used to assay the oligomerization state of the WRAP assemblies.
source: Instead, we used glutaraldehyde crosslinking to assay the oligomerization state of the assemblies (Figure 2C), and confirmed tetramerization for the 2-bladed construct.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological approach.

claim: Glutaraldehyde crosslinking confirmed tetramerization for the 2-bladed WRAP construct.
source: Instead, we used glutaraldehyde crosslinking to assay the oligomerization state of the assemblies (Figure 2C), and confirmed tetramerization for the 2-bladed construct.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result shown in Figure 2C.

claim: SLS data indicated a trimer for the 3-bladed WRAP construct.

claim: The 5-bladed WRAP dimer adopted an unusual, asymmetric structure, hitherto unseen in natural proteins.
source: Rather, the dimer adopted an unusual, asymmetric structure, hitherto unseen in natural proteins (Figure 3D), in which one monomer formed the expected 5 blades of an incomplete propeller, while the other monomer formed only four blades and converted part of the N-terminal fifth blade to a helix, leaving the rest of this blade unstructured.

claim: In the 5-bladed WRAP dimer, one monomer formed the expected 5 blades of an incomplete propeller.

claim: The structural tension resulting from the mismatch between the 7-bladed parent and a 10-bladed assembly is too large to be absorbed at two fragment interfaces.

claim: WRAP constructs yielded two oligomeric propellers with eight blades and one with nine blades.
